title: Top N most-frequent words
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that reads a paragraph of text, counts the occurrences of each unique word (case-insensitive), and prints the top N most frequent words in descending order of frequency. Break ties alphabetically.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program define a structure to group words with their frequencies (e.g., `struct WordFreq`)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Without dynamic lists, grouping associated types in structures is the proper C methodology to keep records organized.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the sorting algorithm correctly sort by count descending, and break ties by sorting alphabetically ascending?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies precise conditional control inside comparison algorithms, testing multi-criteria sorting logic.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program strip punctuation marks (comma, period, exclamation) and convert words to lowercase before comparison?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Standardizing string data is necessary before comparison. Students must filter characters inside a traversal loop.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student fails to handle tied frequencies, printing them in arbitrary order instead of sorting alphabetically.
Student does not strip punctuation, leading to separate counts for 'hello,' and 'hello'.
Student utilizes `qsort` from `<stdlib.h>` with a custom compare function pointer instead of writing a manual Bubble Sort.
Student only prints the words, forgetting to print their corresponding frequency counts.
Student accesses memory outside struct array bounds if the paragraph has more unique words than the array capacity.
